content.text: I reviewed the disclosure, conversation, brief, all four figure briefs, the numeral ledger, and every draft section, tracing each claim limitation and each described structure to affirmative inventor text.

input.summary: Full ledger review completed: all 16 claims (1-10 apparatus, 11-16 method) limitation-by-limitation, all 25 numerals/numbered parts (100-140, 202-216), all four figure briefs and the Brief Description of the Drawings, the title, field, summary, detailed description and abstract were each traced to affirmative USER passages in input/disclosure.md (the conversation is a truncated copy of the same text and adds nothing). Substantially all of the draft traces cleanly: the branch-limit-below-sum premise, per-channel contactor/connector current sensor/control-pilot interface/local connector identifier, upstream branch current sensor as independent safety input, stored authorization/requested current/minimum sustaining current/energy-deficit value, the allocation interval arithmetic (non-charging branch load and configurable safety reserve subtracted from the branch limit), sustaining-first then deficit distribution, pilot send plus connector-sensor verification, reduced pilot command with verification interval followed by one-at-a-time ordered shedding until branch current is below the limit, the three reclosure conditions (zero connector current, connected vehicle reported, randomized recovery delay), welded-contactor recording above a leakage threshold with inhibition of the other contactors and operation of the local fault indicator, network interface with signed local authorization token and last accepted branch limit in nonvolatile memory, outage continuation and the token-gated new-session rule, tamper-evident meter sequence uploaded on return of communication, and the service-input mapping with one low-energy pilot transition at a time stored only on sensor agreement. Numerals are one-to-one with parts, every ledger numeral appears in a figure brief and in the description, no numeral carries two meanings, no section lines exist to cross-check, and no drafting note, placeholder, open question or unresolved alternative remains. Depiction conventions (dashed installation boundary, blank blocks, square contactor outline, circle sensor outline, rounded-rectangle vehicle, diamond decision shapes) are shape-neutral in the claims and description and add no technical assertion; the branch-sensor-upstream-of-all-three-drops placement in FIG. 1 traces to "A branch current sensor measures total current upstream of the connector contactors" read with the subtraction of "measured non-charging branch load", and the FIG. 2 placement of the connector current sensor downstream of the contactor traces to the welded-contactor and zero-current reclosure conditions. One substantive defect was found and is reported twice, once as a source-fidelity defect and once as an internal-consistency defect: the FIG. 2 brief wires the connector current sensor's sensing connection as a branch of the isolated local bus 108, a connection topology the inventor never disclosed (the disclosure puts only "the connector interfaces and contactors" on the isolated local bus), and that wiring contradicts both the detailed description, which deliberately couples the bus to the contactor and control-pilot interface only while stating separately that the controller "is coupled to the connector current sensor 124", and claim 5, which recites the bus as coupling the controller only to the control-pilot interfaces and the contactors. Both findings carry the same filing-clean fix: redraw that segment as a separate sensing connection entering the drawing area, matching the separate sensing-connection convention already used for the branch current sensor in FIGS. 1 and 3.

findings.title: FIG. 2 brief connects the connector current sensor to the isolated local bus, a topology the inventor never disclosed
findings.where: figures/FIG-2.md, paragraph beginning "A solid horizontal line enters from the left of the drawing area" (final sentence)
findings.detail: The figure brief asserts a specific electrical/communication topology: the sensing connection by which the controller reads the connector current sensor 124 is drawn as a branch rising out of the isolated local bus 108, with its junction point on the bus specified relative to the incoming supply line, the contactor branch and the control-pilot interface block. This places the connector current sensor on the isolated local bus. The disclosure enumerates what the bus carries and does not include the connector current sensors: "A controller communicates with the connector interfaces and contactors over an isolated local bus." The only affirmative statement about the controller and the connector current sensor is that the controller "verifies the resulting connector current with the corresponding current sensor" and, for the mapping feature, "confirming the corresponding connector current sensor" — i.e. that a coupling exists, with no statement that the coupling is the isolated local bus or a branch of it. There is no affirmative USER passage placing the connector current sensor on the isolated local bus; the nearest passage is the bus sentence quoted above, which lists only the connector interfaces and the contactors. Connection topology of this kind conveys technical substance (bus loading, isolation boundary, and whether the safety-relevant sensor reading shares the commanded-device bus) and is not a permissible depiction convention.
findings.evidence: Candidate (figures/FIG-2.md): "A further vertical branch rises from the bus line to the lower part of the circle outline of the connector current sensor and represents the sensing connection by which the edge controller reads the connector current sensor; this further branch is a single straight vertical segment, meets the bus line to the right of the incoming supply line and to the right of the branch that rises to the contactor and to the left of the control-pilot interface block". Nearest inventor passage (input/disclosure.md): "A controller communicates with the connector interfaces and contactors over an isolated local bus." — the connector current sensor is not among the devices placed on the bus anywhere in the disclosure.
findings.fix: In figures/FIG-2.md, replace the quoted sentence with a sensing connection that does not originate from the bus line, matching the separate sensing-connection convention already used for the branch current sensor in FIGS. 1 and 3: "A dashed sensing-connection line enters the drawing area from the left below the bus line, crosses the left side of the dashed rectangle in its lower region, runs rightward clear of and below the bus line, and then rises as a single straight vertical segment to the lower part of the circle outline of the connector current sensor, representing the sensing connection by which the edge controller reads the connector current sensor; this line meets no other line work, crosses no other line work, and its two ends are its only contacts with other line work." Make no change to the branch that rises from the bus line to the contactor or to the bus run that meets the control-pilot interface block.

findings.title: FIG. 2 bus topology contradicts the detailed description and claim 5
findings.where: figures/FIG-2.md final topology sentence, versus draft/08-detailed-description.md (FIG. 2 paragraph) and draft/09-claims.md claim 5
findings.detail: The description and claim 5 consistently restrict the isolated local bus 108 to the control-pilot interfaces and the contactors, and state the controller's coupling to the connector current sensor as a separate coupling. The FIG. 2 brief instead branches the connector-current-sensor sensing connection off the bus line, so the drawing would show the sensor on the bus while the text and the claim exclude it. The same draft also treats the branch current sensor connection as a distinct dashed line rather than a bus branch in FIGS. 1 and 3, so the FIG. 2 treatment is inconsistent with the draft's own convention as well.
findings.evidence: draft/08-detailed-description.md: "The isolated local bus 108 couples the edge controller 106 to the contactor 122 and the control-pilot interface 126 of the first connector channel 120. The edge controller 106 is coupled to the connector current sensor 124 of that connector channel and reads the connector current measured by the connector current sensor 124." draft/09-claims.md claim 5: "an isolated local bus coupling the controller to the control-pilot interfaces of the plurality of connector channels and to the contactors of the plurality of connector channels." figures/FIG-2.md: "A further vertical branch rises from the bus line ... and represents the sensing connection by which the edge controller reads the connector current sensor".
findings.fix: Apply the FIG-2.md rewrite given in the preceding finding so the sensing connection to the connector current sensor is a separate line rather than a branch of the bus line. Leave draft/08-detailed-description.md and claim 5 unchanged; they are already source-faithful and consistent with each other.
